chapter: Struttin' Time, chronology and Chicago singers
title: Male impersonators: Seymour and Jeannette, Florence Mills
summary: Jeannette of the team Seymour and Jeannette was a classy male impersonator, as was Florence Mills, whose outfits Lou Leslie kept immaculate.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: But female -- but male impersonators were -- that's completely disappeared. I mean you don't see --
Yeah. Only they have -- they have a show at the Apollo now.
Oh, they do? The Jewelbox Review?
Yeah, they're all male.
But that's female impersonators.
Oh, that's right.
But you don't see male impersonators.
Oh, well now, I tell you the male impersonator that was popular in the early '20's, a girl -- it was a team called Seymour and Jeannette. Jeannette was a male impersonator, but he was Seymour was --
Female impersonator --
No, he was a man.
Uh-huh.

He was a man. He was her husband. But she was a male impersonator, and she was a clever woman, tall, very slender, could sing and dance -- and very classy, very classy, Seymour and Jeannette. Now, you want the female impersonators, don't you?
No, I was just thinking, because I think about, you know, during that period, the '30's, I think of Marlene Dietrich, you know, in her top hat and --
Yes, uh-huh.
It was kind of --
Well, Florence Mills was a male impersonator too, you know.
That's right. She did that too.
Sure she did.
Yeah.
And she was marvelous.
Why was that so popular? I never (inaudible).

I don't know. I don't know, but she was very, very popular, and she looked like a million dollars in her outfit, you know, because Lou Leslie really saw that everything was just to the second for Florence.
